author: /root/l070_publication
claim: A connected simple four-regular graph of girth at least five with a vertex of eccentricity 22 and at most 94 vertices has at most three internal singleton distance layers.
root_and_distinct_checks: The cap bounds for boundary eccentricity at least 4, 5 and 6 are respectively 20, 26 and 32, from disjoint sets of sizes 17+3, 17+9 and 17+15. Only forward distance-layer equalities are used.
Internal singleton positions lie between 4 and 19 and have separation at least four. A backward layer need not consist only of the two backward neighbors.
For a gap of four, the first two interior layers have sizes 2 and 6. The matching and parent labels exclude c=6 and c=7 for the third interior layer.
For c=8,m=1, the double-parent graph has only paths of at most three vertices, so at most five edges instead of seven.
The common-neighbor inequality is 7c+m-29-t <= binomial(c,2). For c=8 it gives t>=1 if m=2 and t=2 if m=3.

For m=2, removing any one of seven labels removes at least one of four possible double-parent edges. The two single-parent vertices give at most four cross edges if nonadjacent, or at most three if adjacent. Both totals are at most seven, below the required eight.
For m=3, each single-parent vertex must have the two reversed double-parent labels avoiding its parent index. Four such vertices and three indices force a quadrangle.
Thus a gap-four section has at least 17 interior vertices; the acquired gap-five bound is 18, and disjoint radius balls give at least 22 for longer gaps.
The exact whole-graph partition is L+R+I+2. The six span/gap rows exhaust spans 12 through 15 and each forces order at least 95.
distinct_challenge_record: J3 independently challenged the common-neighbor inequality, both difficult c=8 cases, the distance-sensitive caps and the exhaustive six-row partition; the checks were sent to root and are recorded above.
attribution: Root supplied the c<=7 argument and a cap observation; l070 supplied c=8 and the complete partition. J3 supplied the distinct challenge. The accepted cap, section and pair-counting proofs are reused.
limits: No argument yet forces four singleton layers.
Graphs with zero through three internal singleton layers remain possible under this theorem.
No retained frontier, cache or execution request is changed.
